description: Draft accessibility plan identifies city barriers.
Proposes actions to improve accessibility for residents.

chips.text: People with disabilities and older adults are the focus.
Consultation with deaf-blind community members is a potential limitation.
Delegate highlighted challenges with screen reader friendly surveys.
Consultations included deaf, Black, cultural, and Indigenous communities.
City plans accessibility audits and expert consultations.

segments.title: Accessibility Plan Report Presentation
segments.takeaway: Staff presented the Accessibility Plan Report, detailing community feedback, identified barriers, and the city's proposed actions across seven domains.

segments.title: Committee Questions on Accessibility Plan
segments.takeaway: Committee members asked questions regarding building audits, staff training, consultation with specific disability communities, and the feedback submission process.

segments.title: Motion to Receive Accessibility Plan Report
segments.takeaway: The committee moved and passed a motion to receive the Accessibility Plan Report and encouraged feedback by September 22nd.

description: Administration will report in January on construction site accessibility.
New ramp styles are being implemented at construction sites.
Recommendations include accessibility for the deafblind community.

chips.text: Recommendations address signals and awareness for deafblind community.

description: Accessible pedestrian signal volumes are too low for blind users.
E-scooter reporting methods are inaccessible for blind/deafblind residents.
Transit platform displays and bins lack accessibility for blind users.

chips.text: Staff confirmed accessible signals automatically adjust volume to ambient noise levels.
Why accessible pedestrian signal volumes are turned down remains unclear.
Blind and deafblind residents face accessibility barriers with city services.
Administration will review signal volume and contact e-scooter companies.
